reader_notes: Read from the note dump (bars 0-84, 2/2, beats are half notes; the subject's anacrusis is the second half of bar 0, which the dump prints as 0:0 and is recorded here as bar 0 beat 2, consistent with the answer at 4:2). Subject taken from SUBJECTS.md (II/13): upbeat E#4 (q. s s ornament) to F#3 at 4:2, 23 notes, real answer. Entries found by interval search on the subject from its first downbeat note and then each read in context; harmony read by hand from the three voices. The project's own entry/cadence analysis was not consulted.

entries.reason: Real answer: exact fifth transposition (B#-C#-G#...), ending C#4 at 8:2 where the bass enters.

Upbeat written out as an ornament (E#5 e F#5-E#5 s D#5 e E#5 e). Exact through B4-A#4 (24:1-1.5); the last two notes G#, F# are not stated in place: the voice leaps to F#5 at 24:2 and the descent A#-G#-F# is spun out in the suspension chain of the next episode (25:1.5 G#4, 26:1.5 F#4).

At the answer's level (C#); since the answer is real, 'answer' only names the level. All pitches present; the tail is rhythmically changed (F#3 q E#3 e D#3 e C#3 e at 36:1-2 for q e e q). Ends C#3 at 36:2 where the alto enters, as in the exposition.
Exact at pitch of bar 0 through B3-A#3 (40:1-1.5); the G# comes an octave high and late (G#4 at 40:2.5, tied, beginning the countersubject against the next entry) and the final F# is omitted.

Subject transposed to D#. In bar 42 it keeps the subject's own intervals (lower neighbour F##4, so a major-mode colouring; C#5 natural = the subject's lowered 7th), but the close is turned to d# minor: G#4 F#4(natural, not F##) E#4 at 44:1-1.75 and the final D# is replaced by F#4 (44:2), the third of the d# chord reached by the IAC at 44:1.
In B major (lowered 7th = A natural at 54:1). Exact through E4-D#4 (56:1-1.5); the last two notes (C#, B) are replaced by the leap to B4 that starts the suspension-chain episode.

Same pitch and much the same texture as entry 2 (bars 8-12; the soprano's countersubject in 65-66 is identical to 9-10). Exact through B2-A#2 (68:1-1.5); the voice then leaps to A#3 and the final G#-F# are dropped.

Two-voice texture (soprano silent 68-76). Ornamented upbeat (B#4 e C#5-B#4 s A#4 e B#4 e), same pitch as the exposition answer. Exact through F#4-E#4 (74:1-1.5); final D#-C# replaced by C#5 at 74:2 (suspension chain).
Final entry, at the pitch of entry 4 (bar 20) but with plain upbeat. Exact through B4-A#4 (80:1-1.5); the voice leaps to A#5 and the closing G#-F# are left to the final cadence.

cadences.reason: End of episode 1: V7 at 19:2.5 (bass C#4, E#4 and B4 above) to I at 20:1 (F#3, F#4, A#4); top voice on ^3. The soprano's subject upbeat follows at 20:2.

Close of the entry in vi: V7 of d# at 43:2.5-2.75 (A#3, C##4, E#5/G#4) to D#3 at 44:1; soprano G#4 suspended over the arrival and resolving to F#4 (^3), alto D#4. The subject's last note is replaced to make this cadence.
End of episode 3: F#7 (bass F#3 at 51:2.5, A#5, C#5/E5) to B at 52:1 (B3 bass, B5 soprano, D#5 alto). The alto's entry in IV begins at 52:2.

Unsure, elided: the link 74-76 arrives on V (bass C#3-E#3-G#3-C#4 at 76:2) and on F#3 at 77:1 with the soprano on F#5, but the soprano's final entry already started at 76:2 and the alto's countersubject holds B4 (a 4th) over the arrival, so the phrase does not really close.
Final cadence: C#4/C#3 at 83:2 (soprano E#5, alto G#4) to F#2, A#4, F#5.

countersubject.description: Syncopated chromatic descent in tied quarters (F#-F#-E#-E-E-D#-D#, at the subject level B-B-A#-A-A-G#-G#) then rising A#-B-D#-E#(h)-F#; about 4:2.5-8:1. Present with entries 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10; absent from entry 9 (two-voice passage).
inversions: octave (fifth below the subject's tonic note becomes a fourth/eleventh above, e.g. 5:1 C#5 over F#4 vs 9:1 B4 over F#3)
double octave / fifteenth (entry 3: twelfth below, 21:1 F#5 over B3)
countersubject.reason: The countersubject lies below the subject in entries 1, 3, 5, 6, 10 and above it in 2, 4, 7, 8, always a fifth below or a fourth above at the subject's first downbeat: invertible at the octave.

notes: No stretto: every entry begins after the previous one has ended (exposition and the 32-44 group link end-to-start). No pedal points (longest held tones are the alto's C#4 at 8:2 and 23:2, about one bar). After the exposition and the bar-32 bass entry, every entry drops or displaces its last two notes (the cadential descent to ^1), handing them to the following episode or cadence; this is a consistent habit of the fugue, not fragmentation. The written-out ornamented upbeat (E# F#-E# D# E#) appears at 20:2 and 70:2. The episodes come in two pairs: 12-20 / 44-52 (imitative 'q. e e e' motive with rising scale) and 24-32 / 56-64 (suspension chain over running bass, rising sequence). Sequence links landing V-i on d# (26:1, 64:1), G# (28:1), C# (60:1) are not counted as cadences; nor are 12:2, 32:2-33:1 and 36:2, where entries arrive on or start from a chord without a phrase close (36:2 C# is heard at once as V of F# for the alto entry). The g# chord at 16:2 is reached by bass ^7-^1 and is passing.
